newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 13.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 13. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Indonesian legal experts have made a fresh call on the government to replace the outdated 1946 Criminal Code with a more sophisticated bill drafted three years ago. The experts said as the Criminal Code did not have provisions on subversion, the government had to use the 1963 Subversion Law, which has been widely condemned as being inhumane.

The government has signaled it was being cautious in deliberating the draft regulation that would give food producers the right to apply "halal" (edible in accordance with Islamic teachings) labels on food products.
Sociologist Arief Budiman said the statement by Transmigration Minister Siswono Yudohusodo that society was sick showed the government's frustration over the recent developments in society.

Armed Forces Commander General Feisal Tanjung said there was a group of people in Indonesia who wanted to create instability. He said the recent riots in East Java, West Java and West Kalimantan had been engineered.
Indonesian badminton players won the doubles and mix-doubles titlew in the Taiwan Open in Taipei on Sunday.
